packets.label: policy
packets.question: Check bounded percent contract, four paths, unchanged business invariants and PENDING bootstrap; mapping vs workflow authority.

packets.label: chain
packets.question: Audit complete caller/selector/plan/manifest/prompt/runner/receipt interfaces and identity consistency. Source extraction internals are reviewed in planner; repair codec and actual reconstruction interface have their own complete-definition packets. No session inheritance.

packets.label: policy-rest
packets.question: Audit remaining contract declarations and limited authority; compare exact source selector and source paths.

packets.label: scope
packets.question: Audit exact repair scope, exclusions, and separation from the future business mission; source allowlist and documentation binding.

packets.label: fixed-table
packets.question: Audit the complete fixed manual table and its use by both actual callers. Questions must cover code, fixtures and cross-module interfaces. No developer PASS or hidden cross-session information.

packets.label: fixed-table-rest
packets.question: Audit the complete literal table in this new-file diff; identity is bound by full Git blob hash. No definitions are truncated; no runtime dependency choices.

packets.label: runner
packets.question: Audit real caller and chunk dispatch, all-prompt preflight, receipt production, failure/retention/cleanup; backend is unchanged trusted component, shown complete invocation interface.

packets.label: backend-bridge
packets.question: Audit backend argv/auth/tool isolation.

packets.label: consumer
packets.question: Audit trusted source reconstruction, manifest and complete diff coverage, actual argv/prompt/completion/session/model/schema checks and aggregation; compare producer interfaces.

packets.label: consumer-rest
packets.question: Audit remaining complete receipt reconstruction, actual prompt/source/session/result checks against the full original protocol; producer/consumer repair interface is separately shown in bootstrap-interface.

packets.label: legacy-v1-byte-compat
packets.question: Compare complete BASE/HEAD definitions to audit unchanged v1 input, manifest and prompt meaning. New repair selection must not alter old calls or historical evidence. Do not use future-model conclusions.

packets.label: planner
packets.question: Audit complete planner and direct pure protocol dependency, Git blob provenance, old v1 and percent-v1, full diff and final prompt cap.

packets.label: planner-rest
packets.question: Audit remaining canonical planner changes, full Git source provenance and final capacity; repair adapter is a separate finite interface, not an arbitrary mission fallback.

packets.label: outer
packets.question: Audit downgrade rejection and actual outer result consumer; unchanged Codex-specific branch remains original authority, not reimplemented.

packets.label: input-consumer
packets.question: Audit complete independent consumer versus complete producer, full definitions/provenance and literal final prompt reconstruction. No generator call is allowed in the consumer.

packets.label: input-consumer-rest
packets.question: Audit remaining independent source/range/prompt reconstruction implementation and producer source reading, including complete definitions, full Git objects and provenance.

packets.label: bootstrap-interface
packets.question: Audit exact repair wiring across selector, plan, fixed producer, real runner, independent reconstruction and receipt consumer. Compare identities, context hashes and actual final input. Codec internals are reviewed in the complete producer/consumer packet.

packets.label: fixed-adapter
packets.question: Audit complete task-only producer versus complete independent consumer, plus exact Manifest and backend prompt template; no new backend, auth, schema or legacy migration.

packets.label: fixed-adapter-rest
packets.question: Audit remaining producer implementation against the complete independent consumer, Manifest and actual backend prompt. All code is visible within this session.

packets.label: mapping
packets.question: Audit all mapping logic: exact pilot identity/four paths, real contract edits/declarations, unknown/mixed-domain rejection; unchanged path classifier included.

packets.label: input-tests
packets.question: Audit source/identity/mode/missing/UTF8/scope/capacity/downgrade tests, complete setup and fixtures; evaluate assertions, not fake PASS as real evidence.

packets.label: runner-tests
packets.question: Audit complete runner/consumer tests with all fake raw/final/argv/session setup. Source behavior is tested separately, not assumed from fake conclusions.

packets.label: downgrade-tests
packets.question: Audit exact-diff/UTF8 tests and nonchunk downgrade at actual outer call; complete fixture setup and relevant full definitions.

packets.label: repair-tests
packets.question: Audit full setup, real fixed-head coverage and all-prompt equality through the actual runner with fake backend. Synthetic output is not a real review.

packets.label: repair-execution-negatives
packets.question: Audit execution-evidence negative cases: full fake receipt/setup and actual consumer/validator, not merely self-consistent JSON hashes.

packets.label: repair-preflight-negatives
packets.question: Audit table/source/range/capacity/downgrade/identity rejection before backend using full test setup and actual gates.

packets.label: physical-consumer-format
packets.question: Audit full durable canonical receipt/raw/final/argv file format and corruption test. Full setup and original file loader plus chunk validator are present. Input codec correctness is a distinct question, not inferred from synthetic PASS.

packets.label: mapping-tests
packets.question: Audit mapping assertions and all body factories; complete mapping implementation. Authorization/mixed assertions have separate interface audit packet.

packets.label: authorization-bridge
packets.question: Audit validate_authorization and mixed-governance assertions in complete pilot test, with full setup; compare precise path categories and existing rules. Mapping assertions are audited by mapping-tests.
